title: HistoPrism: Unlocking Functional Pathway Analysis from Pan-Cancer Histology via Gene Expression Prediction
claim: A staged architecture turns patch embeddings into predictions by conditioning on global context, modeling spatial relations, then regressing targets.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid, left-to-right, QKV attention diagram in panel b
description: A 2x2 grid of rounded panels, (a) to (d), shows the model as a data flow. Panel (a), WSI Preprocessing, shows a histology slide cut into a purple grid. Patches pass through a snowflake-marked (frozen) Feature Encoder and become grey 'img embeddings' boxes. A brown 'Cancer type embeddings' box sits above them. Panel (b), the Cancer-aware Cross-attention Block, shows K, V and Q boxes in yellow, blue and grey. Small colored heatmap grids show attention energy and output, and these lead to cancer-aware embeddings. Panel (c), the Context-aware Self-attention Block, shows embeddings passing through L stacked green Transformer Layers. Panel (d), Gene Prediction, shows a pink MLP producing peach 'gene predictions'. A dashed double arrow labelled Loss links them to orange 'gene expression' ground truth. Grey stacks of embeddings anchor each stage, and the eye starts at the slide image on the left.
caption: HistoPrism architecture. Patch level image embeddings are obtained via pathology foundation models. A cross-attention module injects pan-cancer conditioning. A Transformer Encoder models contextual relations before a final MLP head regresses gene expression values.
abstract: Predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology offers a scalable and clinically accessible alternative to sequencing, but realizing clinical impact requires models that generalize across cancer types and capture biologically coherent signals. Prior work is often limited to per-cancer settings and variance-based evaluation, leaving functional relevance underexplored. We introduce HistoPrism, an efficient transformer-based architecture for pan-cancer prediction of gene expression from histology. To evaluate biological meaning, we introduce a pathway-level benchmark, shifting assessment from isolated gene-level variance to coherent functional pathways. HistoPrism not only surpasses prior state-of-the-art models on highly variable genes , but also more importantly, achieves substantial gains on pathway-level prediction, demonstrating its ability to recover biologically coherent transcriptomic patterns. With strong pan-cancer generalization and improved efficiency, HistoPrism establishes a new standard for clinically relevant transcriptomic modeling from routinely available histology.
